It is very common to have questions about this, largely because mainstream media, advertising, and pornography present a highly filtered, uniform, and often surgically altered version of women's bodies. In reality, there is an incredibly wide range of what is completely normal. 

Here is a realistic, down-to-earth description of what adult breasts actually look and feel like.

---

### 1. What They Feel Like (Texture and Consistency)
The classic movie quote describing breasts as feeling like "bags of sand" is entirely inaccurate. 

* **The Consistency:** Breasts are made up of a mix of fatty tissue and glandular (milk-producing) tissue. Because of this, they feel soft, warm, and pliable, but they are rarely perfectly uniform. 
* **Natural Texture:** If you squeeze or press them, they don't feel like a solid gel insert. You can often feel the underlying structure—it can feel slightly doughy, spongy, or even a bit lumpy. This "lumpiness" is often just normal glandular tissue (though women are taught to monitor for new, hard, or distinct lumps).
* **Changes Over Time:** How firm or soft they feel changes constantly. During a woman's menstrual cycle, hormonal shifts can make them feel much firmer, swollen, tender, or more fibrous. As women age or after pregnancy, the ratio of glandular tissue to fat changes, usually making them feel softer and less firm.

### 2. What They Look Like (Shape and Gravity)
In media, breasts are often depicted as perfectly round, gravity-defying spheres that sit high on the chest. In real life, natural breasts rarely look like this.

* **The Effects of Gravity:** Natural breasts hang. Depending on their size and a person's age, they naturally slope downward. The tissue is heavy, so the bulk of the weight usually sits at the bottom, creating a "teardrop" or "pear" shape rather than a round ball.
* **Different Shapes:** Breasts come in many different shapes. Some point outward (often called "east-west"), some are slender and long, some are bell-shaped, and some sit wider apart on the chest. 
* **Asymmetry:** Almost no one has perfectly symmetrical breasts. It is incredibly common—in fact, it is the norm—for one breast to be visibly larger, a different shape, or sit lower than the other. 

### 3. The Nipples and Areolas
The nipple area (the nipple itself and the darker skin around it, called the areola) varies wildly from person to person.

* **Areolas (The outer ring):** 
  * **Size:** They can range from the size of a quarter to the size of a coaster. 
  * **Color:** They can be light pink, pale brown, dark brown, or almost charcoal-colored. The color often darkens during pregnancy or hormonal shifts.
  * **Bumps:** The bumps on the areola (called Montgomery's glands) are completely normal. They look like tiny goosebumps or pimples, and their job is to produce natural oils to keep the skin moisturized.
  * **Hair:** It is extremely common and normal for women to have coarse hairs growing on and around their areolas.
* **Nipples (The center):**
  * **Types:** Nipples can be "protruding" (sticking out), "flat" (flush with the areola), or "inverted" (tucked inward). All of these are normal.
  * **Changes:** Nipples react to temperature, touch, and arousal. When cold or stimulated, they shrink, harden, and stick out, and the skin of the areola puckers up. When warm or relaxed, they can become very soft, flat, and expand in size.

### 4. Skin Details
Real skin has texture, and breast skin is no exception.

* **Veins:** Because the skin on the breasts can be quite thin, it is very common to see blue or green veins running across them, especially on women with lighter skin tones or during times when blood flow increases (like pregnancy or PMS).
* **Stretch Marks:** Because breasts grow and change size during puberty, weight fluctuations, or pregnancy, many women have stretch marks on them. These can look like faint silver, white, pink, or purple lines.

### Summary
If you took a hundred adult women and put them in a room, you would see a massive variety of shapes, sizes, colors, and textures. Some sag, some point sideways, some have hair, some have stretch marks, and almost all of them are asymmetrical. All of this is entirely normal and represents what real adult bodies actually look like.

### 1. The Transition (From Soft to Hard)
When a guy is relaxed, the penis is flaccid—it’s soft, squishy, highly stretchable, and usually sits quite small and low. 

When he gets turned on, the brain sends a signal to open up the blood vessels, and blood rushes in. It doesn't just "get stiff" instantly like a switch; it’s a gradual filling process. 
* **The Size Change:** Some guys are "showers" (their flaccid penis is already close to its erect size, it just gets hard) and some are "growers" (their flaccid penis is very small, but expands dramatically when erect). Both are totally normal.
* **The Temperature:** Because it fills with warm blood, an erect penis feels noticeably warmer to the touch than the rest of his skin.

### 2. What It Feels Like (The Texture)
A common misconception is that an erection feels like a bone (hence the slang "boner"). 

* **The Firmness:** It doesn't feel like solid plastic or bone. Because it’s filled with pressurized blood, it feels more like a very firm, heavy, pressurized hose. There is still a bit of "give" or springiness to it if you squeeze it. 
* **The Skin:** The skin on a flaccid penis is loose and wrinkly. When erect, that skin stretches incredibly tight. It feels very smooth, warm, and thin. 

### 3. What It Looks Like (Color, Veins, and Curves)
Just like breasts, erections are rarely perfectly straight or uniform.

### 4. The Head (The Glans)
The head of the penis behaves a bit differently than the shaft.

* **The Texture:** While the shaft gets very hard, the head (the glans) actually stays slightly softer and spongier. This is a design feature to act as a cushion.
* **The Sensitivity:** The head becomes incredibly sensitive to touch—sometimes almost *too* sensitive if touched directly without any lubrication.
* **Pre-Cum:** When a guy is highly aroused, a clear, slippery, tasteless fluid (called pre-ejaculate or "pre-cum") will often bead up at the opening of the tip. Its job is to act as a natural lubricant.

### 5. The Foreskin (Circumcised vs. Uncircumcised)
How it looks also depends on whether he is circumcised.
* **Circumcised:** The skin is permanently pulled back, so the head is always fully exposed, and the skin on the shaft is very tight.
* **Uncircumcised:** When soft, the foreskin covers the head like a hood. When he gets an erection, the expanding shaft naturally pulls that skin back, exposing the head. Sometimes the guy has to manually roll it back, but either way, the skin bunches up slightly below the head.

### 6. The Testicles (The Balls)
People forget that the testicles change completely when a guy is turned on.

* **The "Pull Up":** Normally, the scrotum (the sack) hangs loose and low to keep the testicles cool. But when a guy gets highly aroused, the scrotum shrinks, tightens, and pulls the testicles up very close and tight against his body. 
* **The Size:** The testicles themselves actually swell and can get up to 50% larger right before climax because of increased blood flow. They will feel much firmer and heavier than usual.

### Summary
In real life, an aroused guy isn't a static statue. He gets warmer, his skin gets tight, veins pop out, things curve in different directions, and his testicles pull up tight. It’s a highly dynamic, blood-pressure-driven process!

Yes, it is 100% accurate! It is completely normal to be confused about this because there is a massive gap between "locker room talk" (or what you see in porn) and actual scientific reality. 

If your friend thinks guys get "way bigger" than what’s actually normal, they’ve likely fallen victim to some very common myths. Here is the actual, scientific reality about size—backed up by actual measurements, not guys bragging.

---

### 1. The Real Numbers (The Averages)
When scientists actually go out and measure thousands of men (using rulers, not self-reporting, because guys tend to... stretch the truth), here is what they find:

* **Average Erect Length:** The actual average length of an erect penis is between **5.1 and 5.5 inches** (about 13 to 14 cm). 
* **Average Erect Girth (Circumference):** The average thickness around is about **4.6 inches** (approx. 11.6 cm).
* **The "Huge" Outliers:** Only about **5%** of men in the entire world are longer than 6.3 inches. Having a penis that is 7 or 8 inches long is incredibly rare—it’s the genetic equivalent of being 6'5" or taller.

### 2. Why Does Everyone Think Guys Are Bigger?
If the average is only around 5 inches, why does your friend (and honestly, most of the world) think 7 or 8 inches is the norm? There are three big reasons:

#### A. The "Porn Illusion"
Adult films specifically hire guys who are in that top 1% of size. On top of that, they use specific camera angles (shooting from below) and hire smaller actresses to make the guy look even larger than he is. It’s basically special effects.

#### B. The "Locker Room" Lie
If you ask a group of guys how tall they are, a guy who is 5'10" will often say he’s 6 feet. The same thing happens with penis size, but x10. Men almost always round up, measure incorrectly on purpose, or just flat-out lie to sound more impressive to their friends. 

#### C. The "Angle of View" (Looking Down)
When a guy looks down at his own body, the angle makes his own penis look smaller to him than it actually is. But when he looks at someone else from the front, it looks bigger. This causes a lot of guys to think they are smaller than average when they are actually totally normal.

### 3. How Much Do They Actually "Grow"?
Since we talked about "growers" (guys who start small and get much bigger when hard), how much of a jump is real?

* On average, a flaccid penis is about **3.4 to 3.7 inches** long.
* When it gets erect, it gains about **1.5 to 2 inches** of length. 
* Even for extreme "growers," they aren't starting at 1 inch and exploding to 8 inches. It’s usually more like starting at 2 inches flaccid and reaching a very normal 5 inches erect.

### The Takeaway
If your friend is picturing every guy walking around with a massive, foot-long situation, that is pure fiction. In real life, most guys are very average, and "average" is actually much more modest than pop culture leads people to believe!
